title: Idę czy chodzę?
title_en: iść vs chodzić · now vs regularly
note: Direct sequel to a2_jechac and the pack that finally closes a1_motion. TWO JOBS: (1) the full present of isc -- ide, idziesz, idzie, idziemy, idziecie, ida -- which a2_jechac deliberately reserved for this node, so its discrimination was live at ja and ty only; (2) the habitual partner chodzic. The now-vs-habit split carries the intro's weight exactly as jechac-vs-isc did in the previous unit, because English 'go' covers both and gives him nothing to hang it on. Load is kept to one new SYSTEM: isc is the -e/-esz class he already owns (chciec, jechac) and its id-/idzi- stem split is presented as the same table fact as ja-/je-, never as a rule; chodzic is the -e/-isz class he owns from mowic, lubic, robic. Adverbs do the semantic work: teraz (already taught) vs codziennie (NOT in the taught pool -- this pack teaches it, tagged in teaches_lemmas, introduced on slide 1 in an all-known frame Codziennie pije kawe so it is never a second unknown). FENCED, must not appear: the habitual counterpart of jechac (the by-vehicle verb) is not named, glossed, hinted at or used as a distractor anywhere in this file, note included, so the intro never opens that door -- which is why slide 3 borrows jechac only for its ENDINGS and says nothing about jechac having a routine partner of its own; ALL past forms of both verbs; all prefixed motion verbs. FORKS TAKEN: (a) the unit has 14 forms (2 infinitives + 12 present) and Dopasuj is capped at 12, so the board is the 12 present forms, 6 isc + 6 chodzic, perfectly balanced and drilling the exact contrast; the infinitives isc/chodzic are carried by the intro grids plus a Kontrola item each, which satisfies the every-form-taught rule via intro. (b) codziennie is production-demanded across Uzycie, so it gets its own Pisanie item rather than riding on the intro alone; that makes Pisanie 13. (c) my/wy cannot take a noun subject, so those four Uzycie items are adverb + destination (two of them questions, which AGENTS exempts); the other ten carry real noun subjects (tata, mama, dzieci). (d) present tense carries no gender, so the both-gender production rule has nothing to bite on here -- it belongs to the fenced past. NOTE FOR THE HUMAN: the POOL.md handed to this build was regenerated at END OF a2_feelings (node 55) but this node is 72, with twelve live nodes in between; dzieci, rodzice and i are taught at a2_plural_nom / a2_family2 / a2_past_plural and are legal here.

intro.title: One English word, two Polish verbs
intro.body:
English lets you say I go and I'm going almost interchangeably. Polish will not. There are two different verbs, and you choose by WHEN it happens:

- On the way right now → idę. You have had this one since Idę do sklepu.
- Something you do again and again → chodzę. That is the new word.

One small word first. codziennie means every day, and it sits in a sentence like the time words you already use: Codziennie piję kawę. = Every day I drink coffee.

Now the pair. Same shop, same feet, same do + genitive — only the timing changes, and the timing changes the verb.
intro.body_pl: Teraz = idę. Codziennie = chodzę. Po obu: do + dopełniacz.

intro.title: iść — the full grid
intro.body:
The dictionary form is iść — to go on foot. You have owned idę and idziesz since your first do-phrases; here are the other four, and now the verb is complete.

Read the two shapes straight off the table: id- in idę and idą, idzi- in the four in the middle. That is simply how the word is built — exactly the way jadę and jadą sat outside the je- block last time.
intro.body_pl: Bezokolicznik: iść. Dwa kształty: id- (idę, idą), idzi- (środek tabeli).

intro.title: iść uses endings you already own
intro.body:
iść is in the -ę/-esz class — the same class as chcieć and jechać. Put the two motion verbs side by side and every ending matches, line for line:

-ę · -esz · -e · -emy · -ecie · -ą

Listen to the bottom line especially: jadą, idą. The they-forms rhyme. Nothing on this slide is new — only the stem is.
intro.body_pl: iść = klasa -ę/-esz, jak jechać i chcieć. Te same końcówki, inny temat.

intro.title: chodzić — the regular-habit verb
intro.body:
chodzić means to go somewhere again and again, on foot — a routine, not a trip you are on right now. It belongs to the other class you already own: the -ę/-isz class of mówić, lubić and robić.

Watch the top and bottom lines. lubię and lubią keep their i; chodzę and chodzą do not — the same shape as płacę. Take it from the table; there is nothing to work out.
intro.body_pl: chodzić = klasa -ę/-isz, jak lubić i mówić. Uwaga: chodzę, chodzą (bez i).

intro.title: Which one? Let the time word decide
intro.body:
Nothing else in the sentence moves — not the subject, not the destination. Only the verb tells your listener whether this is happening now or happens always.

A test you can use out loud: if teraz fits, use iść. If codziennie fits, use chodzić.
intro.body_pl: Pasuje teraz → iść. Pasuje codziennie → chodzić.

examples.en: Right now Dad is on his way to work.
Dad goes to work every day.
The children are on their way to the park right now.
The children go to school every day.
Are you going to the shop? (right now)

quiz.prompt: Right now I'm on my way to the shop →
quiz.explain: teraz means this is happening as you speak, and that is what iść is for. chodzę would tell your listener you do it as a routine, which is a different piece of news.

quiz.prompt: Every day I go to the park →
quiz.explain: codziennie is a routine word, so the routine verb has to follow it. Polish will not let you use idę here even though English says the same word both times.
tata is a he, and the he-slot in the -ę/-isz class is bare -i — the same slot that gives lubi and mówi.

quiz.prompt: Tata ___ do pracy. (he is on his way now)

quiz.explain: dzieci is plural, so you need the they-form. idą is the second of the two id- forms — it rhymes with jadą, which you already know.

quiz.prompt: The children go to school every day →
quiz.explain: Two things at once: plural subject gives the they-form, and every day gives the routine verb — chodzą.

quiz.prompt: we're on our way home (right now) →
you (plural) go to the office every day →
to go on foot — dictionary form →
quiz.explain: The dictionary form looks almost nothing like the present tense — iść, but idę and idziesz. Nothing to derive; the grid is the thing to know.

quiz.prompt: to go regularly, on foot — dictionary form →

quiz.explain: The person is right and the destination is right; only the verb is wrong. codziennie says routine, and routine is chodzić territory.

type_items.explain: The plain -e ending of this class, the one that also gives chce and jedzie. The stem is idzi-, so the two run together as idzie.
Back to the short id- stem, just as jadą went back to ja-. The table starts and ends with the short shape.
The -ę here is written with no i in front of it, unlike lubię. Compare płacę — same shape.
-isz is the badge of this class. If a verb has -isz here, it will have -imy and -icie further down — lubisz, mówisz, chodzisz.
No i before the -ą, matching chodzę at the top. lubią and mówią keep theirs; this verb does not.

use_items.prompt_en: Type: Right now I'm going to the shop.
Type: Every day I go to the park.
use_items.explain: Same park, same feet as the sentence above — but codziennie makes it a habit, and Polish keeps a separate verb for habits.

use_items.prompt_en: Type: Right now Dad is going to work.
Type: Dad goes to work every day.
use_items.explain: The pair to the sentence above. Only the verb tells your listener whether Dad is out of the door now or does this every morning.

use_items.prompt_en: Type: Mum is going to the pharmacy right now.
Type: Mum goes to the shop every day.
Type: The children are going to the park right now.
use_items.explain: dzieci is plural, so the verb is the they-form idą — the short id- shape, the one that rhymes with jadą.

use_items.prompt_en: Type: The children go to school every day.
Type: Are you going to the shop? (right now)
Type: Do you go to the park every day?
use_items.explain: English needs a different question shape for the habit — do you go, not are you going. Polish changes the verb instead and leaves the question alone.

use_items.prompt_en: Type: We're going home right now.
Type: We go to school every day.
Type: Are you (plural) going to the bank right now?
Type: Do you (plural) go to the office every day?
